solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Pelt spy’s family (8)

blocks.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation; MOLE'S without the apostrophe
kin = family

annotation.surface: An instruction to skin the relatives of a secret agent.
annotation.walkthrough: The possessive does real work: spy's family is MOLE'S KIN, read straight through as one word.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the fur of a mole, once prized for waistcoats, is itself a pelt.

entries.clue: Complete dosser’s no longer burning for drink (3-3-3)

indicators.note: one thing given 'for' another means it takes that thing's place

blocks.note: a dosser, someone sleeping rough, is a down-and-out; the 's is 'is'
to down = to drink; this is the part that goes
a fire that is out has stopped burning; it replaces DOWN

annotation.surface: A tramp who has given up drink and fire, told off as a complete dosser.
annotation.walkthrough: The dosser is not the answer but its near neighbour DOWN-AND-OUT; swap its DOWN (drink) for OUT and the phrase shifts to meaning complete.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a rogue through and through is a complete, thorough one.

entries.clue: Monster cycling over tail of stricken American animal (7)

indicators.note: cycling a word moves its last letter round to the front
the tail of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: to monster is to scold severely (Australian slang) = CHIDE; cycled, the final E comes to the front
last letter of stricken
A = American

annotation.surface: A monster riding a bicycle over the end of a stricken American creature.
annotation.walkthrough: Monster looks like a noun, and Echidna is even a monster in Greek myth, but here it is the verb 'to scold', CHIDE.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the spiny anteater of Australia and New Guinea is one kind of animal.

entries.clue: School meal? (5)

blocks.note: the surface pushes a classroom; the setter means a school of whales
not a canteen lunch but what those whales eat

annotation.surface: What's on the menu in the school canteen?
annotation.walkthrough: School is the collective noun for whales, and krill is what they feed on; the question mark flags the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: Whales swim in schools, and the tiny crustaceans they filter from the sea are their meal.

entries.clue: Cuckoo egg (3)

blocks.note: cuckoo as a noun = a fool, a nitwit shortened
the egg of a louse, found in hair

annotation.surface: The cuckoo's egg, the one it lays in another bird's nest.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pairs the words as bird and egg; each is instead a separate definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a silly person (short for nitwit), and the egg a louse lays in hair.

entries.clue: Tone of medic gripped by fatigue (6)

indicators.note: the medic is held inside the word for fatigue

blocks.note: tire = fatigue (verb)
MB = Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor

annotation.surface: The weary voice of a doctor worn out by the job.
annotation.walkthrough: Medic is the crossword's usual doctor abbreviation, and 'tone of medic' tempts a reading about bedside manner; tone alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the tone colour that distinguishes one voice or instrument from another.

entries.clue: Male holding nerve, partly in charge of systematising classes (9)

indicators.note: the male holds the nerve part inside him

blocks.note: a tom is a male cat
an axon is part of a nerve cell
IC = in charge

annotation.surface: A man showing some nerve while running a system of classifying school classes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nerve, partly' is a definition by example: an axon is one part of a nerve, not a letter selection.
annotation.definitionFit: Adjective for taxonomy, the science of sorting living things into ranked classes.

entries.clue: One’s arresting oafish Aussie for contempt (7)

indicators.note: one word catches and holds the other inside it

blocks.note: one's = my, speaking of oneself
an ocker is a boorish, uncultivated Australian

annotation.surface: A police officer arresting a loutish Australian for contempt of court.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Contempt' looks legal in the surface, as if someone were arrested for contempt of court; it is plain scorn.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: ridicule expresses contempt, and the two are used interchangeably.

entries.clue: Continued with chapter in Animal Farm (5)

blocks.note: a show that ran on continued
CH = chapter

annotation.surface: A reader pressing on with the next chapter of Orwell's novel.
annotation.walkthrough: The capitals dress it as Orwell's book; read plainly it is a farm for animals.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: an American farm where cattle or horses are raised.

entries.clue: State of the art, but periodically returned (4)

indicators.note: take letters at regular intervals
the selected letters come back the other way

blocks.note: the even letters of tHe ArT bUt give HATU, which is then read backwards

annotation.surface: A grudging remark that something is state of the art, but with a catch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'State of the art' is a set phrase that hides the split: State is the definition and the fodder starts at 'the'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Mormon heartland, capital Salt Lake City, is one of the fifty US states.

entries.clue: Keen on writer after kiss, empty talk and booze? (10)

indicators.note: the writer comes after the kiss

blocks.note: to be into something is to be keen on it
X is the kiss at the end of a letter
the writer is the setter, I
cant = hollow, insincere talk

annotation.surface: A writer fond of kisses, idle chatter and drink.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks booze as one example of an intoxicant.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example, flagged by the question mark: alcohol is one thing that intoxicates.

entries.clue: Tiny blonde novel writer (4,6)

indicators.note: novel = new, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

annotation.surface: A petite fair-haired author of novels.
annotation.walkthrough: Novel sits between the fodder and 'writer' to look like a kind of writer, but it is the anagram signal. Enid Blyton was a prolific English children's author (the Famous Five, Noddy).
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Famous Five author is one writer among many.

entries.clue: Tell sir about climbing frame (7)

indicators.note: the letters are moved about

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: Telling a teacher about the playground climbing frame.
annotation.walkthrough: Climbing frame suggests a playground; the climber here is a plant.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a garden lattice up which roses and clematis climb.

entries.clue: Part of speech, touchingly genuine (4)

indicators.note: the answer is part of the following words

blocks.note: the last three letters of speech plus the first of touchingly, across the comma

annotation.surface: A part of a speech that was touchingly sincere.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Part of speech' reads as a grammar term; here it just means the answer sits in the word speech and runs on.
annotation.definitionFit: A German loanword used in English to mean authentic, the real thing.

entries.clue: Study plants wild bison eat (8)

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters will not stay in their given order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A field note: observe the plants that wild bison eat.
annotation.walkthrough: Wild looks like it describes the bison; it is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a verb for collecting and examining plants in the wild.

entries.clue: Dreadful monster, in private (9)

indicators.note: the letters are dreadfully jumbled

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Someone who is a dreadful monster behind closed doors.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In private' reads as a phrase, but 'in' belongs to the fodder and 'private' stands alone.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: deepest thoughts are the ones kept private.

entries.clue: Large numbers leaving northern border in chaos (6)

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the letter for northern departs from the word it was in

blocks.note: MANY without N (northern)
a hem is the border of a garment

annotation.surface: Crowds fleeing the northern frontier amid chaos.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a refugee scene; 'northern border' splits into N and a sewing hem.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: violent disorder, originally a legal term for maiming.

entries.clue: All one’s possessions on credit, including a vehicle (6,3)

indicators.note: to include something is to take it in, so the credit abbreviation takes the A inside itself

blocks.note: a person's estate is everything they own
CR = credit, in accounts
A itself, inside CR

annotation.surface: Someone buying a car on credit with everything they own.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On credit' reads as a hire-purchase deal; credit is just its accounting abbreviation. An estate car is British for a station wagon.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the British name for a station wagon, one kind of vehicle.

entries.clue: Part of flower cultivated in tin (6)

indicators.note: the cultivated word goes in the tin

blocks.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
tame = cultivated, domesticated

annotation.surface: A flower grown in a tin pot.
annotation.walkthrough: Cultivated sounds like gardening or an anagram signal; it is TAME, which sits between S and N.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the pollen-bearing male organ is one part of a flower.

entries.clue: Whit Monday’s beginning with Charlie in disgrace (7)

indicators.note: the beginning of Monday is its first letter
Charlie goes in the disgrace word

blocks.note: first letter of Monday
odium = disgrace, public hatred
C is Charlie in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A Whit Monday spent with a disgraced Charlie.
annotation.walkthrough: Whit Monday is the British bank holiday after Pentecost, and it hides the split: whit, a tiny amount, is the definition. C sits between ODI and UM.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both mean a tiny amount, as in 'not a whit' or 'a small measure of sense'.

entries.clue: Secure tax cut (8)

blocks.note: to lace a shoe is to secure it
a rate is a local tax

annotation.surface: A government promise to lock in a tax cut.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tax cut' reads as one phrase; the join falls between them, and cut is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to tear flesh raggedly is to cut it.

entries.clue: Left with speed after right old romp (7)

indicators.note: left and speed come after right and old

blocks.note: R = right
O = old
L = left
to go at a lick is to go at speed

annotation.surface: A political swerve from right to left, hurried along into some old frolic.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue lists left-with-speed first, then says it comes after right-old.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both mean to frolic boisterously.

entries.clue: Small sweet potato (4)

blocks.note: S = small, as in clothing sizes
pud is British slang for pudding, a dessert or sweet

annotation.surface: A little sweet potato.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sweet potato' is a real vegetable, so the eye takes it as one; sweet is a pudding and potato stands alone.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: the everyday slang word for a tuber.

entries.clue: Floor covered with rubbish and crumbs (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, KO has PAN on top of it

blocks.note: to pan a show is to rubbish it
to floor someone is to knock them out, KO

annotation.surface: A kitchen floor strewn with litter and crumbs.
annotation.walkthrough: Floor and rubbish look like nouns for mess; both are verbs, knock out and criticise.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Japanese-style breadcrumbs used for crisp coatings.

entries.clue: Laughing king replaces leader in prominence (10)

indicators.note: the king takes the leader's place

blocks.note: visibility = prominence, being noticed
the leading letter of VISIBILITY, which goes
R = rex, king; it replaces the V

annotation.surface: A king who laughs as he takes over from the leader in a position of prominence.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leader' is not a separate person but the first letter of the prominence word.
annotation.definitionFit: The noun for a readiness to laugh, so the definition works as a noun, laughing.

entries.clue: Airline with 100 staff (5)

blocks.note: BA = British Airways
a ton is slang for a hundred

annotation.surface: An airline with a hundred employees.
annotation.walkthrough: Staff looks like employees; it is a stick.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a conductor's or relay runner's short stick is a kind of staff.

entries.clue: Storyteller dictates first couple of notes in the wrong order (10)

indicators.note: take the first two letters
the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder
first two letters of notes

annotation.surface: A storyteller dictating the opening notes out of sequence.
annotation.walkthrough: DICTATES plus NO, ten letters in all, are jumbled.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: one who tells short amusing tales is a storyteller.

entries.clue: One starts to study Monroe Doctrine (3)

indicators.note: take the starts of the next words

blocks.note: I = one, the Roman numeral
first letters of study and Monroe

annotation.surface: A student beginning to study the Monroe Doctrine.
annotation.walkthrough: The Monroe Doctrine is the US policy opposing European meddling in the Americas; the famous phrase is broken, and Doctrine alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: any distinctive doctrine or theory, from the suffix of words like Marxism.

entries.clue: The very thing children desire (4)

blocks.note: 'it' = the very thing, as in 'that's it!'
CH = children

annotation.surface: Exactly what children want.
annotation.walkthrough: Desire looks like a verb for the children; it is a noun, the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: a restless craving is felt like an irritation of the skin.

entries.clue: Quip from toff about half-cut parent (3,3)

indicators.note: to turn about is to face the other way, so the toff's letters are read backwards
the parent is cut in half

blocks.note: a nob is a toff, a posh person; NOB turned round
MOTHER with half its letters cut

annotation.surface: A posh wit's remark about his tipsy mother.
annotation.walkthrough: Half-cut is British slang for drunk, which is the picture; here it halves MOTHER.
annotation.definitionFit: French loanword for a witty remark, literally 'good word'.

entries.clue: Handles twinkling new president with extremes of resourcefulness (8)

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

blocks.note: in a twinkling = in a mo, a moment
N = new
Ike = Dwight Eisenhower, US president
first and last letters of resourcefulness

annotation.surface: A report of a sparkling new president full of resourcefulness.
annotation.walkthrough: Handles looks like a verb; as a noun it is slang for names.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: a handle and this word both mean a person's name.
